newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs have little faith in banks - survey.
newsitem.headline: Czechs have little faith in banks - survey.

text.p: A series of major problems at some Czech banks in 1996 battered overall faith in financial institutions, but confidence recovered slightly at the end of the year, an opinion poll released on Monday said.

The survey by the state Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM) in early December showed 38 percent of Czechs had faith in the country's banks and financial institutions, up from 19 percent in October when the survey was first conducted.
Distrust remains very strong. IVVM said 52 percent of the citizens showed distrust in banks, but that was down from 74 percent in October.
The survey was taken among 993 Czechs aged 15 and older.
Several smaller Czech banks were put under central bank administration or shut last year, bruising the sector's image.

The problems peaked in September, when the fifth largest bank, Agrobanka a.s., went into forced administration because of low liquidity connected to the failure of a smaller Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank is currently searching for a majority shareholder to take control of Agrobanka which was connected to Kreditni through an obscure investment firm called Motoinvest.
The failure of Kreditni, which investigators said was caused by dubious debt-swap deals linked to Motoinvest, in turn caused a crisis in confidence in Agrobanka.

Agrobanka was the 12th and so far the largest Czech bank to have been subjected to central bank intervention, since post-Communist liberalisation of the sector created dozens of new banks in the early 1990s.
But the central bank stresses that more than 70 percent of banking activity in the country is conducted with the so-called "Big Four" banks.
The CNB last autumn set up a multi-billion crown programme for the 13 remaining small private banks, offering to buy back non-performing debt, through the state-run Konsoliacni Banka.
Analysts praised the move as a preventative strike against potential instability in the banking sector.
